newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hardleft says put tax evasion before welfare.
newsitem.headline: Italy hardleft says put tax evasion before welfare.

text.p: Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation party wants action against tax evasion to precede any discussion by the government on welfare spending reform, a senior party official said on Wednesday.
Paolo Ferrero, the party's spokesman on welfare issues, said it was "intolerable" that tax evasion was 10 times higher in Italy than the European average.

"The government must take concrete action... to end this scandal. For us communists the discussion and the adoption of concrete acts on combatting tax evasion is therefore preliminary to any discussion on social spending," he said in a statement.
Refoundation ensures the centre-left government's majority in the lower house of parliament.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday the government's annual document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF) would set out strategies for reforming the pensions system.

"The problem of the welfare state regards pensions above all. There are doubts that the pensions system even after reforms, may not be balanced in the medium term. For this reason it will be necessary to intervene," he said.
The government has placed welfare reform high on the agenda as it fights to straighten out public finances and win a place in Europe's planned currency union.
It faces opposition from trade unions and the Communist Refoundation to make any changes before 1998.
